rites.name: Vesyushora
rites.text: Vesyushora is a concept in Oriamora, a force of arcane will that the orders of the Holy Age bound into the doors between worlds. It was first named during the Courts, when councils argued over whether a concept could be held at all. Its power is a steady pull that bends flame and bends the doors toward a single purpose.

rites.name: Silemuarla
rites.text: Silemuarla is a concept of the Arcane Realm of Oriamora, a current of gathered flame that the temple orders of the Holy Age learned to bind into vows. It was born in the Fall, when worlds split in the Sundering and their broken pieces became Shards, and it is said to hold the oath that the Pact was sworn upon.

rites.name: Amilornum
rites.text: Amilornum is a concept in Oriamora's Arcane Realm, born in the Fall when the Sundering broke worlds into Shards. It is sworn into the Pact, a binding that the temples of the Holy Age keep alive through flame and ritual.

rites.name: Orolus
rites.text: Orolus is the concept of a sundering tide that runs through the Arcane Realm of Oriamora, pulling fractured worlds toward a shared horizon during the Fall. In the Age of Sundering its currents were said to carry the oaths of the Pact across broken shores. Scholars still debate whether it was a force, a memory, or a promise kept by the shards.

rites.name: Nuala
rites.text: Nuala is a concept of the Arcane Realm in Oriamora, a binding-principle that gave the Walled Age its shape of holding walls, sworn orders and early churches. In the Age of the first sovereign it is said to have hallowed the groves where the first growing kingdoms took root.

rites.name: Amillia
rites.text: Amillia is the concept of a binding oath in Oriamora's Walled Age, the promise that holds stone to stone and a sworn people to their sovereign. It is felt most strongly where walls are raised over generations and where the first crossings were made between warring groves.

rites.name: Vorouzhurn
rites.text: Vorouzhurn is a concept in Oriamora's Walled Age, a principle that a holding wall keeps its strength only while the order that raised it keeps its vows. Its adherents set the first crossings of the Holy Age by binding flame to stone, so the energy of a sworn wall is paid out only once and then stored again in the next vow. The concept is taught in temples as a measure of how much one covenant can carry before it gives way.

rites.name: Silimys
rites.text: Silimys is an arcane mechanism of Oriamora's sixth era, a lattice of brass-threaded sigils that lets a wearer press the hours of a day into a longer working span before the lattice demands its rest. Its keepers claim the lattice draws its surplus from the slow turning of tidal ley-currents beneath the old quarries.

rites.name: Drare
rites.text: Drare is a concept born in Oriamora's Arcane Realm, the notion of a branching ending that the Library of the Three Futures shelves alongside every other outcome. It was first named during the Age of the first sovereign, when groves and growing kingdoms were the chief forms of order, and its meaning shifts with each reader who consults the shelves.

rites.name: Sethiazith
rites.text: Sethiazith is the concept of branching endings in Oriamora, the principle by which every unrealised future is shelved in the Library of the Three Futures. During the Holy Age of flame, temples and orders, its scribes hold that a single choice can be read forward through all its consequences at once.
